title: Histograms
author: 696637e49d26457b33c7eff3
chapter_outcomes: Know the difference between an ungrouped and a grouped frequency distribution, and understand the advantages and disadvantages of combining data into a grouped frequency distribution. Variables in groups defined by, for example, 30 – under 40, 30 ⩽ x < 40.

Identify class limits, boundaries, midpoints and widths for a grouped frequency distribution. For discrete data, class limits, boundaries, midpoints and widths will be required. For continuous data, class boundaries, midpoints and widths will be required.
Represent a grouped frequency distribution as a histogram and interpret a histogram. Histograms with unequal class widths will have the vertical axis labelled 'frequency density'.
Represent a grouped frequency distribution as a frequency polygon and interpret a frequency polygon. Groups will have equal class widths. Including comparing a pair of frequency distributions.
Form a cumulative frequency distribution from a frequency distribution and vice versa.
Represent the cumulative frequency distribution of a continuous variable as a cumulative frequency polygon or curve, and interpret a cumulative frequency polygon or curve.
